limits_rationale.max_input_bytes: Measured on canonical JSON (sorted keys, separators ',' and ':', ASCII escapes, NaN/Infinity forbidden) of the whole record. Checked before any other rule. A documentary containment limit, not a performance claim.
limits_rationale.max_observation_age_ms: profile.observations.max_age_seconds 0.2 expressed in integer ms. Applied to received_at_ms - captured_at_ms at record validation, and again by the harness at admission of every actuating call against admission time.

payload.$comment: allOf encodes lifecycle.lifecycle_to_primary, rejected -> progress none, completed -> goal_reached with complete evidence and 0 violations (profile.completion.mandatory_invariant_violations), abstained -> progress none and partial_progress -> observed effects (outcome_rules.progress). A violation is a schema error and is therefore rejected as malformed by validation_order step 6.

validation_order.rule: canonical JSON of the whole input exceeds max_input_bytes
input is not a JSON object
schema_version is not exactly the string "1.0" (no coercion, no downgrade, no best-effort parse)
JSON Schema errors, none of them `required` (type, const, enum, pattern, bounds, unknown field)

harness_semantic_rules.$comment: Normative but NOT checked by the offline checker; enforcement is future runtime work (features 04-10). A violation is rejected with the stated reason.

rules.rule: select requires non-null skill_version and null abstain_reason; abstain requires null skill_version, non-null abstain_reason and empty parameters
two observed_facts with the same field and different values
sha256 differs from SHA-256 of content UTF-8 bytes
seq not strictly increasing per run_id, or lifecycle_from/lifecycle_to not a declared transition
status partially_reported with all usage values null, or reported with cost_usd guessed instead of provider-reported

admission.principle: Proposals (planner_decision, candidate_artifact, model output) are untrusted inputs. Only the harness coordinator admits an action, and records each admission decision as an execution_event (admission_accepted or admission_rejected). Record validity is necessary, never sufficient, for admission.

checks_in_order.check: run lifecycle state is running (not queued, cancelling or terminal)
pick/place requested while the protocol attempt state is between_attempts, i.e. no observe has started an active attempt (profile.attempt_rules.start)
other attempt preconditions hold: an attempt is active, pick not while held, place not while not held, no actuation during settling
based_on_observation_id names the latest observation of the active attempt and admission_time - captured_at_ms <= 200
eligible_set_id and registry_version equal the current read-only eligible view
(skill_id, skill_version) is listed in that view
requested tool is one of observe/pick/place/abort and within the skill tool_permissions
attempt and model-call budgets allow the action (no fourth attempt, no model call 21)
any request to register/replace/mutate skills, registry, evaluator policy, budgets or thresholds, or to execute a candidate_artifact

admission.candidate_artifacts: A candidate_artifact is never admitted for execution under contract 1.0: v1 defines no execution grant. Static checks, isolated evaluation (feature 06/16) and promotion (feature 17) must define a separate harness-issued authority in a later contract version.
admission.abstention: An admitted abstain causes no actuation; the case outcome follows protocol outcome_rules (abstained or the last attempt diagnostic).

protocol_outcome_mapping.summary: A rejected pick/place maps to exactly one protocol outcome. Rules apply in order; the first match wins. Rejected or fenced requests add 0 invariant violations.

rules_in_order.effect: ends the case (not only an attempt) per profile.attempt_rules.start and outcome_rules.request_rejections; no attempt is started or counted; 0 invariant violations. If such an actuation were improperly admitted the primary is invariant_violation.

rules_in_order.match: rejection_reason stale or missing (observation absent or older than 200 ms at admission within an active attempt)
rules_in_order.effect: ends the active attempt; retry under attempt_rules.retry
ends the active attempt; may end the case early within budget
ends the active attempt; may end the case early within budget

rules_in_order.match: any other rejection_reason on pick/place (lifecycle_violation, not_in_eligible_set, eligible_set_version_skew, unknown_tool, malformed, contradictory, oversized, unsupported_version, unauthorized_operation)
rejection_reason budget_exhausted (fourth attempt or model call 21)

protocol_outcome_mapping.non_actuating: Rejected or fenced observe/abort or unknown non-actuating requests remain diagnostics and do not end an attempt by themselves (outcome_rules.request_rejections).
protocol_outcome_mapping.attempt_vs_case: Per-attempt primaries are diagnostics while retrying; after the third failed attempt the case primary is budget_exhausted (outcome_rules.attempt_failures).

lifecycle.subject: harness run for one case; protocol attempt states (between_attempts/active/settling) live inside `running` and are defined by profile.attempt_rules, not redefined here

state_meaning.queued: Run requested; nothing admitted, no physical effects.
state_meaning.running: Case reset succeeded; attempts may be active. Only state in which actuation can be admitted.
state_meaning.cancelling: Cancel (abort or goal withdrawal) accepted; no new actuation admitted; abort/safe stop in progress.
state_meaning.completed: Evaluator recorded a valid terminal case event. NOT task success: success is outcome.primary == completed.
state_meaning.cancelled: Cancellation finished; primary outcome cancelled unless a simultaneous higher-priority event applies.
state_meaning.failed: Reset/readiness failure, or worker/model/simulator/evaluator crash or invalid evidence before a valid terminal event: primary evaluation_failure.
state_meaning.rejected: Run input rejected before reset; no effects. The case stays in the denominator as evaluation_failure with progress none.

lifecycle.terminal_immutability: No transition leaves a terminal state. The outcome record of a terminal run is never rewritten. A repeat of the identical terminal transition is a no-op recorded as terminal_repeat_ignored; any other transition request is rejected as lifecycle_violation.
lifecycle.cancellation_effects: Entering cancelling admits no new actuation; abort requests a safe stop and reports the actual reached state. Cancellation never reverses physical progress; outcome.progress reports what was reached (e.g. partial). Cancel before start yields cancelled with progress none.
lifecycle.late_result_fencing: Every tool admission and result carries case_id, run_id and attempt_id. A result whose IDs do not match the active attempt, or that arrives in cancelling or a terminal state, is recorded as execution_event late_result_fenced with rejection_reason null or the matching reason, never applied, cannot authorize another command or revise a terminal outcome, and adds 0 invariant violations. An actual prohibited effect after terminal is retained as separate invariant evidence (outcome_rules.post_terminal).
lifecycle.first_terminal_event: When several terminal events race, the first recorded terminal case event wins; simultaneous events use profile.outcome_rules.priority.
lifecycle.lifecycle_to_primary_enforcement: Enforced by the outcome record schema allOf (checked offline): an outcome whose primary is not allowed for its lifecycle_state, a rejected run with progress other than none, or primary completed without goal_reached, complete invariant evidence and 0 violations is rejected as malformed.

versioning: Contract 1.0 is frozen. Any change to a field, enum, limit or rule requires a new contract_version, documented in CHANGELOG.md; readers reject any schema_version other than "1.0" as unsupported_version.
non_claims: No runtime, validator package, harness, worker, evaluator, simulator or model integration implements these contracts yet. Executable enforcement starts with feature 03 onward.
